business_summary.text: Fedbank Financial Services Limited is a systemically important non-deposit-taking NBFC registered with the RBI, classified as an Investment and Credit Company, lending across products and geographies.

call_points.text: FY27 AUM growth guidance held at 20-25% even assuming flat gold prices.
Weighted average cost of borrowing held flat at 7.80% for a fourth quarter.
GNPA rose to 1.8% from 1.6% and Stage II to 3.6%, which management attributed to the gold loan periodic-interest construct, not credit loss.
On a 50 bps rate hike, management said it cannot pass on all of it and will offset via opex and credit cost levers.
Asked to guide on gold yields, management declined, calling Q3 an intense market.
Insurance income was about 0.1% of the ROA tree in FY26, sold only to LAP customers, not gold loan borrowers.
Credit cost for FY26 stood at 0.8% and is expected to remain range-bound in FY27.
Doorstep gold loan AUM expanded to ₹1,730 Cr in FY26 compared to ₹830 Cr in FY25.

operating_notes.text: Loans stood at ₹14,318.85 Cr at Mar-2026 against ₹11,646.37 Cr a year earlier.
The company transferred ₹605.02 Cr of loans not in default through assignment in Q4FY26, retaining 10% beneficial economic interest.
The company has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture as at March 31, 2026.
Gold loan portfolio LTV stood at 60.9% in FY26.
Average ticket size for retail installment loans originated in Q4 FY26 was ₹34.3 lakh.
98.9% of AUM is secured against property or gold.
AUM stood at ₹20,153 Cr at Mar-2026, up 27.5% YoY, with Q4FY26 disbursements of ₹11,665 Cr.
Credit cost for Q4FY26 was 0.7%, and FY26 credit cost was ₹115.3 Cr against ₹216.4 Cr in FY25.
Branch count was 757 across 17 states and union territories at Mar-2026, with 34 new gold loan branches added in Q4FY26.
Loans stood at ₹16,02,001 lakh at Sep 30, 2026, up from ₹14,31,885 lakh at Mar 31, 2026.
CRAR was 20.96% at Sep 30, 2026 against 20.71% at Jun 30, 2026.
The company transferred ₹87,689 lakh of loans not in default through assignment during the quarter, retaining 10% beneficial economic interest.
Q2FY27 credit cost was 0.6% of average assets, with absolute credit cost of ₹27.1 Cr against ₹31.5 Cr a year ago.
Branch count was 831 across 18 states and union territories at Sep-2026, up from 757 at Jun-2026.
Net gain on direct assignment was -₹1.2 Cr in Q2FY27 against ₹6.6 Cr in Q2FY26.
Gold loan AUM per branch fell to 16.9 Cr in Q2FY27 from 17.7 Cr, which the filing attributes to opening 74 new branches.
Off-book AUM was 26.2% of total AUM at ₹16,264 Cr in Q2FY27, up from 27.2% a year ago.
Gold loan portfolio LTV was 60.9% in Q2FY27 versus 67.9% a year ago.
Gold loan AUM per branch stood at ₹16.9 Cr after the branch additions, with gold tonnage up 16% YoY and LTV at 68%.
Small ticket LAP approval rates recovered to mid-40% from about 30% while coming out of the woods on credit cost.
Medium ticket LAP holds yields of about 11.5% to 12.5% and is described as a steady, profitable business.
